definitions.gloss: right in the middle of, in the thick of
definitions.explanation: Emphasizes being at the peak or most intense point of an activity or situation. Stronger than {最中|さいちゅう} alone.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう}だ。
examples.english: We're right in the middle of a meeting.

examples.japanese: {今|いま}、{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう}で{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: I'm busy right now — I'm in the middle of moving.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}が{満開|まんかい}の{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう}に{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってしまい、お{花見|はなみ}ができなかった。
examples.english: It rained right when the cherry blossoms were in full bloom, so we couldn't have a flower-viewing party.

notes:
USAGE:
An emphatic form of {最中|さいちゅう} (in the middle of). The {真|ま}っ prefix intensifies the meaning, stressing that the activity is at its peak or most intense moment. Used in the pattern ～の{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう} (right in the middle of ~).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事|しごと}の{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう}: right in the middle of work
- {食事|しょくじ}の{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう}: right in the middle of a meal
- {試合|しあい}の{真|ま}っ{最中|さいちゅう}: right in the middle of a game

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最中|さいちゅう}: in the middle of (less emphatic)
